text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman promised his host President Arpad Goncz that both ethnic Hungarians and Croats will be able to return to their homeland in Slavonia in a month's time once the Croatian law and order is restored.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said his talks with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad focused on bilateral relations, investment opportunities, trade ties and co-operation in other areas. The Malaysian Premier also raised the possibility of Hungary and Malaysia co-operating in Bosnian reconstruction.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs exchanged diplomatic notes with his Japanese counterpart Ikeda Yukihito in Tokyo on Monday regarding the scrapping of visa requirements.

- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze disagreed with Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar in Bratislava on Monday on the implementation of tasks set down in the Hungarian-Slovak basic treaty, particularly those relating to ethnic Hungarians in Slovakia.

- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti received a pledge on Monday from the Romanian Premier that officials from the Hungarian Defence Ministry will be permitted to lay a wreath on October 6 this year at the monument in Arad.

- Minister in charge of civil secret services Istvan Nikolits announced on Monday that neither Socialist MP Gabor Kiss nor any other MP has any kind of confidential relationship with the Intelligence Office.
- The parliamentary group of the Free Democrats unanimously elected Istvan Szent-Ivanyi to the post of parliamentary group leader on Monday, effective May 1.
- Laszlo Nyikos, vice-president of the State Audit Office (ASZ), has been nominated by a parliamentary committee to the post of ASZ president.

- The Vienna-based Central Wechsel- und Creditbank, which is wholly owned by the National Bank of Hungary, may post losses as a result of a $15.68 million loan which the borrower, the Panama-based Enavest Holding, failed to pay back by the June 1996 deadline, the Austrian weekly Profil reports.
- The BUX index approached the magic 6,000 point mark on Monday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Anthony Cragg, Deputy NATO Secretary-General responsible for defence planning, told Defence Ministry Deputy State Secretary Istvan Gyarmati in Budapest on Monday that Hungary has achieved much more in defence planning than officials in Brussels had expected.

- Pig farmers have suffered combined losses of two billion forints so far this year. The poultry market has partially collapsed as domestic consumption has dropped 10 percent over the last few months.
- Based on a February government decree, the State Privatisation and Holding Co. is set to privatise Raba in two stages this year.
- An environmental protection information centre, part of the Global Resources Information Database founded by the United Nations Environmental Protection Programme opened in Budapest on Monday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Health Insurance and Pension Insurance Funds had outstanding debts to collect of 226.6 billion forints in early April.
- Primagaz had after-tax profits of 1.57 billion forints on sales of 17.63 billion forints last year, according to International Accounting Standards.
